findings.description: No test checks that an exact key beats a wildcard that also matches. The only exact-key case (`'@ui'`) has no competing wildcard, so moving `const exact = aliases.get(specifier); if (exact) return exact;` after the wildcard loop would still pass. Add a case such as `{ "@*": ["b/*"], "@ui": [...] }` that resolves `'@ui'` to the exact target.

The `parsePathAliases` JSDoc ("A `paths` or `baseUrl` of a shape tsc rejects throws") and ADR 0130 overstate the shape check. `"paths": [["src/*"]]` passes `Object.entries` as the alias `"0" -> ["src/*"]`, and an empty substitution list `"@a/*": []` is kept without throwing, though tsc rejects both. Neither does any harm, but the text should say that only the shapes that throw fall back to no aliases.

`parsePathAliases` computes the bounds, enforces them and builds the Map in one function, and the bound names hide what they count. `size` is entries plus substitutions, and `chars` is a three-term formula in which `baseChars` stands in for `join(baseUrl, t)`. Rename them (`entryCount`, `aliasChars`) or extract a small `withinAliasBounds` predicate.

The 10-line JSDoc above the `MAX_PATH_ALIAS_*` constants walks through the cost arithmetic term by term ("Each bound caps one term of what an import costs…"), which the code in `parsePathAliases` already states. Keep the WHY (the merge lock that no stage timeout reaches, decisions 31 and 110) with one line per constant, and drop the cost narration.
